steps.title: Why Short Reviews Help
steps.prompt: 글의 중심 생각으로 가장 적절한 것은?
steps.passage: Many students read a new word several times and feel certain that they know it. However, seeing a word is not the same as recalling it without help. A short quiz can reveal what the learner can actually remember. Reviewing the same material on different days also offers a useful challenge: the learner must bring the information back after some forgetting has occurred. This does not mean every review should be difficult. When a student makes a mistake, a clear explanation and another chance to answer can make the next attempt more useful. Over time, a series of short reviews may be easier to maintain than one very long study session.
choices: 긴 공부 한 번이면 복습은 필요 없다.
짧은 회상 연습과 간격을 둔 복습이 도움이 될 수 있다.
단어는 소리 내어 읽기만 하면 충분하다.
오답을 피하기 위해 쉬운 문제만 풀어야 한다.
steps.explanation: 단순히 읽는 것과 스스로 떠올리는 것이 다르며 여러 날에 걸쳐 짧게 복습하는 장점을 설명한다.

steps.title: Five Minutes That Stayed
steps.prompt: 다음 글의 중심 생각으로 가장 적절한 것은?
steps.passage: At the beginning of the semester, Hana made a plan to study English for one hour every evening. She followed it for two days, but soon other homework made the plan difficult. Instead of giving up, she changed the plan to five minutes of vocabulary review after breakfast. Five minutes seemed too short to make a difference, yet it was easy to repeat. After three weeks, she had practiced on more days than in the previous month. She did not suddenly know every word. However, she felt more confident because studying had become part of her routine. Her teacher asked her to track the days she actually practiced, not the length of her most impressive session. The record made her consistency visible. A small habit that lasts can be more useful than a perfect plan that quickly disappears.
choices: 복습보다 숙제를 먼저 포기해야 한다는 주장
아침 식사가 영어 학습보다 중요하다는 주장
오래 지속되는 작은 학습 습관의 가치
한 번에 오래 공부하면 모든 단어를 외울 수 있다는 주장
steps.explanation: 글의 논지를 요약하면 ‘오래 지속되는 작은 학습 습관의 가치’이다. 근거: A small habit that lasts can be more useful than a perfect plan that quickly disappears.
steps.evidenceQuote: A small habit that lasts can be more useful than a perfect plan that quickly disappears.

steps.passage: A volunteer at a small cultural museum noticed that visitors often skipped the longest labels. She asked the audience which information they actually wanted. Visitors began asking more questions instead of walking past.

steps.prompt: Although로 시작하는 절은 어떤 관계를 나타내나요?
steps.english: Although the expense was high, the local council wanted to improve the environment.
steps.explanation: although는 앞의 상황에도 불구하고 뒤의 일이 성립함을 나타냅니다.

steps.title: 문장을 연결해요

steps.explanation: if절은 뒤의 일이 성립하는 조건을 제시합니다.

steps.title: The Short Ride
steps.passage: Our local bus company wanted more people to ride its weekend bus. Posters showed comfortable seats, yet few passengers came. Drivers asked residents about the problem. The bus left before the market opened and returned before shoppers finished. The company changed the schedule without buying new buses. More people used the service because it now matched their plans.
choices: 운행 시간이 주민들의 일정에 맞게 바뀌었다.
steps.explanation: 시간표를 바꿔 주민들의 계획과 맞아졌기 때문에 이용이 늘었습니다.
steps.evidenceQuote: More people used the service because it now matched their plans.

steps.title: Keeping the Hall Comfortable
steps.passage: During a school event, every available heater was switched on. The room soon became too warm, and the extra expense worried the organizer. A student measured the temperature in several places instead of guessing from one corner. Two heaters were enough to provide comfort across the room. The remaining heaters were turned off, reducing the energy the event would consume.
steps.explanation: 한 지점의 느낌이 아니라 여러 장소의 측정값을 이용했습니다.
steps.evidenceQuote: A student measured the temperature in several places instead of guessing from one corner.
